corrections: Mapped the Whack-a-Hole source folder to whack_a_mole.

before: Whack-a-Mole is a single-player real-time reaction and clicking game. The player uses the left mouse button to click moles that randomly appear from a fixed 3 × 3 set of holes within a 30-second time limit.

At any time, at most one mole is visible. A mole appears at one of the 9 fixed holes and remains visible for a limited duration. Clicking a visible mole awards points according to its type, immediately removes the mole, and starts a short waiting period before the next mole appears.
after: Whack-a-Mole is a single-player real-time reaction and clicking game. The player uses the left mouse button to click moles that randomly appear from a fixed 4 × 4 set of holes within a 30-second time limit.

At any time, at most one mole is visible. A mole appears at one of the 16 fixed holes and remains visible for a limited duration. Clicking a visible mole awards points according to its type, immediately removes the mole, and starts a short waiting period before the next mole appears.

before: The area contains 9 fixed holes arranged in 3 rows × 3 columns:
after: The area contains 16 fixed holes arranged in 4 rows × 4 columns:

before: At the start of the game, all 9 holes are visible, no mole is visible, Score is 0, Time is 30, and the game waits 0.3 seconds before spawning the first mole.
after: At the start of the game, all 16 holes are visible, no mole is visible, Score is 0, Time is 30, and the game waits 0.3 seconds before spawning the first mole.

before: The main game objects and state variables include the 9 holes, Normal Mole, Golden Mole, current mole, score, countdown, mole-related timers, and game state.
after: The main game objects and state variables include the 16 holes, Normal Mole, Golden Mole, current mole, score, countdown, mole-related timers, and game state.

before: The game contains exactly 9 fixed holes arranged in a 3 × 3 layout. Each hole has a size of 100 × 70 px and remains at its fixed position throughout the game.
after: The game contains exactly 16 fixed holes arranged in a 4 × 4 layout. Each hole has a size of 100 × 70 px and remains at its fixed position throughout the game.

before: The hole is randomly selected from all 9 fixed holes. Two consecutive moles are allowed to appear at the same hole; the previous hole is not excluded from the next selection.
after: The hole is randomly selected from all 16 fixed holes. Two consecutive moles are allowed to appear at the same hole; the previous hole is not excluded from the next selection.

before: The game always uses the same 9-hole layout. Hole positions never change during gameplay.
after: The game always uses the same 16-hole layout. Hole positions never change during gameplay.

before: 2. Randomly select one of the 9 holes.
after: 2. Randomly select one of the 16 holes.

before: At initialization, the game creates the interface and 9 fixed holes, sets Score to 0 and Time to 30, clears the current mole, initializes all mole-related timers, enters `playing`, and starts a 0.3-second initial waiting period.
after: At initialization, the game creates the interface and 16 fixed holes, sets Score to 0 and Time to 30, clears the current mole, initializes all mole-related timers, enters `playing`, and starts a 0.3-second initial waiting period.

before: During `playing`, the bottom instruction area displays `Click the mole` and `Restart: R`. When Time reaches 0, the game enters `game_over`, the current mole disappears, Score stops changing, and the bottom area displays `Game Over` and `Press R to Restart`.
after: During `playing`, the bottom instruction area displays `Click the mole` and `Restart: R`.
When Time reaches 0, the game enters `game_over`, the current mole disappears, Score stops changing, and the bottom area displays `Game Over` and `Press R to Restart`.
